newsitem.title: FRANCE: Right's majority slips in BVA French poll.
newsitem.headline: Right's majority slips in BVA French poll.

text.p: Following are the results of an opinion poll of voters' intentions ahead of the May 25/June 1 two-round parliamentary election.
The telephone poll of 2,036 adults was conducted by BVA on May 15 and 16 for Europe 1 radio, France 2 television and Paris Match magazine and made public on Saturday.
Voting intentions were calculated on the basis of those who said they were certain to vote, or 70 percent of the sample.
Of those who were certain to vote, 12 percent did not express a preference.
The projection of seats in the National Assembly covers the 555 constituencies in metropolitan France, not the 22 seats in overseas departments and territories.
A previous BVA poll conducted on May 9-10 gave the centre-right coalition government and its supporters 303 seats against 226 seats for the Socialist party and its allies.
